title: JavaScript Introduction
summary: JavaScript tells the browser what to do. Show a message, add two numbers and change the words on a page.
introduction: A recipe tells you how to make a snack. A program tells a computer what to do, step by step. JavaScript is a language we use to write those steps. You can try the first examples right here. There is no need to install a coding tool.
learningObjectives: Use JavaScript to add two numbers
Change a heading after the browser has made it

blocks.text: The **console** is a place where a program can show messages. `console.log` asks it to show something. Put words inside quote marks.
Step 2: Use code as a calculator
`2 + 3` is a maths step, so it has no quote marks. `"I have"` is text, so it has quote marks. The program follows the lines from top to bottom.
Step 3: Give a value a name
A **variable** is a name for a value. Here, `points` starts as 3. The next line adds 2 and saves the new value. The last line shows 5.

items: `id="greeting"` gives this heading a name on the page.
`document.getElementById("greeting")` finds the page part with that name.
`textContent` is the text inside it. The code changes that text.
The script is below the heading. The browser makes the heading before the script tries to find it.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: Code must find a page part before it can change it. A script above the heading may run too early. Also, JavaScript cares about letter case: write `console.log`, not `Console.Log`.

blocks.title: Your turn
blocks.text: Change the message to your first name. Then change the two numbers in the calculator example. Guess the answer before you run it.

seo.title: JavaScript Introduction – What It Is and Your First Script
seo.description: Learn what JavaScript is for, how it works with HTML and CSS, where scripts go in a page, and how to print and read values with console.log.
